overview:
**High fire danger continues today, driven by low humidity (24%) and dry 1000-hr fuels, though scattered afternoon storms bring a slight cooling trend.**
- Danger stays "High" through Sept. 3, with ERC easing midweek before climbing back to 88% by Sept. 3.
- Minimum humidity of 24% met the local watchout threshold (1 of 7 flagged) despite 0.01" of rain and light NE winds.
- No Red Flag Warning is posted; NWS calls for 30–40% storm chances through Saturday with gusty winds.
- Stage 1 fire restrictions remain active on BLM Uncompahgre-area lands covering Montrose, San Miguel, Ouray and Delta counties, plus part of Gunnison County.
- Nearby: the Gold Mountain Fire two miles north of Ouray is 87% contained at 39,734 acres, with energy infrastructure threatened and area closures in place.
- The Elk Fire near Lake City is 52% contained at 7,257 acres, with minimal fire behavior and structures still threatened.
